title: forward: new opt-in `failover RCODE…` option (1.13.0) — no behaviour change by itself

detection.reason: an additive option: nothing in the snapshot changes meaning at 1.13.0, so there is no object to name

quote: plugin/forward: No failover to next upstream when receiving SERVFAIL or REFUSED response codes
remediation: Nothing changes at 1.13.0 unless you set it: forward never retried the next upstream on a SERVFAIL/REFUSED answer (only on transport errors and timeouts), and the new `failover SERVFAIL REFUSED` option opts a forward block into doing so. Add it where a flaky primary should be masked by the next upstream. `next` is a different feature (it hands the query to the next forward plugin).
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*forward\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed forward block may opt into rcode failover with failover SERVFAIL REFUSED from 1.13.0

title: grpc: DNS message size limits are enforced
quote: plugin/grpc: Enforce DNS message size limits
remediation: Oversized messages through the grpc backend are rejected from 1.13.0; backends returning very large answers need truncation handling.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*grpc\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed grpc upstream is subject to the size limits

title: geoip: missing latitude/longitude will stop being reported as 0

detection.reason: what consumes the geoip metadata (templates, log formats) is a Corefile value

quote: Users relying on 0 as a sentinel value should update their logic before this change takes effect.
remediation: Templates or log formats that treat `0` as "unknown location" must handle an empty string instead before the next release.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*geoip\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed geoip block's missing coordinates change from 0 to empty

title: auto: zone-file regex length is limited

detection.reason: the regex is a directive-line argument, which is not collected

remediation: From 1.13.2 the auto block's directory regex is capped at 10000 characters (plugin/auto maxRegexpLen) and a longer one is rejected at Corefile load. Real-world regexes are far below the cap; only generated ones need a look.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*auto\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed auto directive's regex is length-checked

title: multisocket: the number of sockets is capped

detection.reason: the socket count is a directive-line argument, which is not collected

quote: plugin/multisocket: Cap num sockets to prevent OOM
remediation: A `multisocket` count above the new cap is clamped/rejected from 1.13.2; check the configured value.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*multisocket\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed multisocket directive is subject to the cap

title: sign: invalid UTF-8 in the dbfile is rejected

detection.reason: zone data files are not collected

quote: plugin/sign: Reject invalid UTF‑8 dbfile token
remediation: Zone files with non-UTF-8 bytes fail to sign from 1.13.1; clean them up.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*sign\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed sign block's dbfile must be valid UTF-8

title: forward: a failover option listing NOERROR is rejected — CoreDNS does not start

detection.reason: the rcodes listed after `failover` are Corefile values; only the option key is projected

remediation: Remove NOERROR from the `failover` option of forward blocks (only forward blocks that use failover are named). From 1.13.2 the parser reports `NoError cannot be used in failover` and CoreDNS exits at startup.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*failover\\b.*\\bNOERROR\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed failover line lists NOERROR, which 1.13.2 rejects at startup
